clue.text: Felt shocking (ate rotten game)

indicators.note: something rotten has decayed and fallen apart, so the letters before it collapse into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written; it looks like a second anagram signal but is fodder
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone felt dreadful after eating game meat that had gone off.
explanation.walkthrough: The brackets make 'ate rotten game' look like an aside about bad meat; ignore them. 'Shocking' tempts as an anagram signal, but all fifteen letters of the first three words are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: King of the Castle is a children's playground pastime in which one player holds a mound against the others.

clue.text: Linesman back ultimately worries

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so only the final letter of the word is kept

blocks.note: the last letter of 'back'
what is eating you is worrying you

explanation.surface: A football linesman at the back of the field frets about his decisions.
explanation.walkthrough: A linesman here is a writer of lines of verse, a crossword favourite for a poet; John Keats is the Romantic poet.
explanation.definitionFit: Keats wrote poetry, line by line, so the crossword sense of a person who writes verse lines fits him.

clue.text: Compositions turns once mangled

indicators.note: something mangled is crushed out of shape, so the letters lose their original order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A musician's pieces are spoilt by a performance that once went badly wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: The nine letters of the two middle words are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Nocturnes are dreamy pieces of music, like Chopin's piano works, so they are musical compositions.

clue.text: I’m old, contrary and beginning to tire and forget

indicators.note: contrary means running the opposite way, so the letters are read backwards
the beginning of a word is its opening letter, so only that is kept

blocks.note: taken as written, apostrophe dropped
O is the standard abbreviation for old
the first letter of 'tire'

explanation.surface: An awkward elderly person admits to getting tired and forgetful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Contrary' looks like a description of the grumpy old person, but it only turns the first two pieces round; the tire letter is added after.
explanation.definitionFit: To omit something is to leave it out, which is what you do when you forget to include it.

clue.text: Trump’s top motive for betrayal

indicators.note: the top of a word written downwards is its first letter, so that one is kept

blocks.note: the first letter of 'Trump'
a motive is a reason for doing something

explanation.surface: A political jibe asking what really drives a famous president to betray people.
explanation.walkthrough: The president's name is just a source for its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Treason is the crime of betraying one's country, so it is a grave form of betrayal.

clue.text: Inlet into which sound flows?

blocks.note: surface reading: a sea channel, a Sound, flowing into a bay or creek
setter's reading: the opening in your head through which noise enters

explanation.walkthrough: A sound is also a strait of sea water, so this reads as geography; the question mark flags that the inlet is anatomical and the sound is noise.
explanation.definitionFit: The opening of the outer ear is where noises go in, an informal word for the ear's entrance.

clue.text: A Republican chap in a state

blocks.note: taken as written
R is the abbreviation for Republican
a gent is a man
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Republican man finds himself in a state, either an American one or a fluster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In a state' looks like the end of the wordplay or an idiom for agitation, but 'in' and 'a' are letters and 'state' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Argentina is a sovereign South American country, and a country is a state.

clue.text: West Indian trade really is not inspiring leaders

indicators.note: leaders are the ones out in front, so each word gives up its opening letter

blocks.note: the first letters of these five words

explanation.surface: A Caribbean commentator laments that commerce in the region is uninspiring.
explanation.walkthrough: The first letters of five consecutive words spell the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Trini is the informal name for a person from Trinidad, an island in the Caribbean.

clue.text: Electric vehicle reversing on eco-friendly plant

indicators.note: a car reversing goes backwards, so the letters that follow are read the other way

blocks.note: EV is the standard abbreviation for an electric vehicle
RE means on, as in regarding
green means environmentally friendly

explanation.surface: An electric car backs into a green power station.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reversing' seems to describe the vehicle, but it turns 'on' (RE) around; 'plant' means a growing thing, not a factory.
explanation.definitionFit: An evergreen is a shrub or tree that keeps its leaves all year round.

clue.text: King to open a herb store

indicators.note: to open something you get inside it, so one piece goes into the middle of the other

blocks.note: R is short for rex, Latin for king
taken as written
chives are an onion-flavoured herb

explanation.surface: A monarch is invited to cut the ribbon at a new herb shop.
explanation.walkthrough: The king's letter goes in after the first letter of 'a chive', splitting the phrase open.
explanation.definitionFit: An archive is a place where records are kept, so it is a store of documents.

clue.text: Music mag that’s printed on paper

indicators.note: what is printed on something is placed after it in an across answer, setting the order of the parts

blocks.note: a rag is a newspaper, usually a poor one
Time is a well-known news magazine

explanation.surface: A music magazine that still appears in print rather than online.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Music mag' looks like one phrase, but 'Music' is the definition and the magazine is one piece. A rag is a disparaging word for a newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: Ragtime is a syncopated piano style from early twentieth-century America, a genre of music.

clue.text: Conservative cuts problem for dregs of society

indicators.note: a cut goes into something, so one piece is inserted inside another

blocks.note: C is the abbreviation for Conservative
a sum is a maths problem

explanation.surface: Tory spending cuts create hardship for the poorest in society.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cuts' reads as a political noun, but it is a verb: the party letter cuts into the arithmetic problem.
explanation.definitionFit: Scum is a contemptuous word for the most worthless people, the lowest layer of the social order.

clue.text: Aunts doing wrong is surprising

indicators.note: something gone wrong has come out badly arranged, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: It is a shock when respectable aunts misbehave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doing' looks like part of the phrase 'doing wrong', but it is fodder with 'Aunts'.
explanation.definitionFit: Astounding means amazing or startling, a stronger synonym for something unexpected.

clue.text: Business trouble

blocks.note: first meaning: a firm or commercial enterprise
second meaning: worry or anxiety

explanation.walkthrough: The two words read like one phrase about a firm in difficulty, but each is a separate meaning of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun names both a commercial company, as in a going concern, and a feeling of worry or unease.

clue.text: Spanish region in stupor turning centre to left

indicators.note: turning the middle into something else swaps that one letter for a new one

blocks.note: catatonia is a state of stupor, so someone in a stupor is catatonic
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A dazed region of Spain shifts its politics leftwards.
explanation.walkthrough: The centre letter of the nine-letter stupor word is its fifth, a T, which becomes L.
explanation.definitionFit: Catalonia is an autonomous community in north-east Spain, with Barcelona its capital.

clue.text: Remove main elite with a reshuffle

indicators.note: a reshuffle mixes things into a new order, as cards or cabinet posts are mixed

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A prime minister clears out the top ministers in a cabinet reshuffle.
explanation.walkthrough: The nine letters of the two middle words are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: To eliminate something is to get rid of it completely, so it means take away or remove.

clue.text: Isle in record book or digest

indicators.note: something in something else sits inside it, so one piece goes within the others

blocks.note: an EP is an extended-play record
I is the abbreviation for isle
a tome is a large book

explanation.surface: Someone hunts for an island's name in a record book or an abridged guide.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Digest' looks like a verb or a magazine, but it is a noun meaning summary.
explanation.definitionFit: An epitome is a summary or abstract of a longer work, which is what a digest is.

clue.text: Manipulator manipulating a photo set

indicators.note: manipulating means handling and moving about, so the letters are worked into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone doctors a set of photographs to deceive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Manipulator' suggests a schemer, but here it is someone who manipulates bones and joints.
explanation.definitionFit: An osteopath treats patients by moving and pressing their bones, muscles and joints with the hands.

clue.text: A way to stop row: being better at fighting

indicators.note: a stopper is pushed into an opening, so one piece is plugged inside another

blocks.note: taken as written
ST is the abbreviation for street, a way
a tier is a row of seats

explanation.surface: Advice on ending a quarrel: be the tougher fighter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' looks like a quarrel, but it is a line of seats. In British slang a tasty person is handy with their fists.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang calls a hard, capable brawler tasty, so the comparative describes someone more formidable in a scrap.

clue.text: Soldier in uniform …

blocks.note: first meaning: a professional member of the standing army
second meaning: even, consistent, the same throughout

explanation.surface: A soldier dressed in uniform, whose sentence carries on into the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In uniform' reads as dress, but 'uniform' is an adjective meaning even. The ellipsis just joins the surfaces of this clue and the next.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a full-time professional soldier and also describes something steady and evenly patterned.

clue.text: Austere hospital admits person with cut

indicators.note: something cut is shortened, so the word loses its final letter
to admit is to let in, so one piece is taken inside another

blocks.note: a san is a sanatorium, a kind of hospital
a party is a person, as in the guilty party

explanation.surface: A spartan hospital takes in a patient with a wound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With cut' suggests an injury, but it shortens the legal word for a person by one letter before it goes inside the hospital.
explanation.definitionFit: Spartan describes a plain, harsh way of life, named after the famously disciplined ancient Greek city.

clue.text: … found brilliant place to retreat

indicators.note: to retreat is to go back, so the letters run in the opposite direction

blocks.note: a star is a brilliant performer, or a brilliant light
to place something is to put it

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue: the soldier found a fine spot to fall back to.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Found' looks like the past tense of find; it is the verb meaning establish. The ellipsis links the surface to the previous clue only.
explanation.definitionFit: To start up a company or organisation is to establish it, the present-tense sense of found.

clue.text: King possibly following guiding star

indicators.note: what is following comes after, so this piece is placed second

blocks.note: guiding means leading the way
a king is a chess piece, and chess pieces are men

explanation.surface: A monarch, perhaps a Magus, follows a guiding star to Bethlehem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Guiding star' looks like one phrase about the Magi; it splits, with 'star' the definition. 'King possibly' points to a chessman.
explanation.definitionFit: The leading man in a film or play is its principal male actor, the star of the show.

clue.text: Leaning close to wall, up to no good outside

indicators.note: the close of a word is its end, so its final letter is kept
one piece placed outside another wraps around it

blocks.note: someone at it is up to mischief
the final letter of 'wall'

explanation.surface: A troublemaker loiters near a wall, leaning on it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At it' is British slang for misbehaving, as in the kids are at it again.
explanation.definitionFit: Atilt means tilted or inclined to one side, an adjectival way of saying at a slant.

clue.text: Places one might go in Battle

blocks.note: first meaning: toilets, where one goes when nature calls
second meaning: a 1915 First World War battle in northern France

explanation.surface: Tourist spots to visit in Battle, the Sussex town.
explanation.walkthrough: Battle is a real town in East Sussex, so the capital disguises the war. 'Go' is a euphemism for using the toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: Loo is British for lavatory, and the Battle of Loos was a major British offensive of 1915.

clue.text: Jet that produces wind without resistance

indicators.note: without means lacking, so a letter is taken away from the word

blocks.note: Brussels sprouts are notorious for causing flatulence
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: A jet engine that makes a gust with no drag.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jet' and 'wind' suggest aircraft or weather; the wind is the digestive kind.
explanation.definitionFit: A spout is a stream of liquid forced out, as from a whale, which is a jet of water.

clue.text: Composer’s rotten, as Queen might’ve said!

indicators.note: this points to how the word comes out in a cut-glass royal accent, its pronunciation rather than its spelling

blocks.note: food that is rotten has gone off; in a plummy upper-class voice the word sounds longer

explanation.surface: The Queen pronounces a composer's work dreadful.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is 'is'. The late Queen's clipped vowels made 'off' sound like 'orf'. 'Queen' here means the monarch, not the band.
explanation.definitionFit: Carl Orff was the German composer best known for the choral work Carmina Burana.

clue.text: A good article about sometimes surly author

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the preceding letters are read backwards
sometimes means now and then, so only every other letter is kept

blocks.note: taken as written
pi is short for pious, meaning good
an is the indefinite article
the second and fourth letters of 'surly'

explanation.surface: A decent piece about a writer who could be grumpy.
explanation.walkthrough: V. S. Naipaul, the Trinidad-born Nobel laureate, had a reputation for prickliness, so the surface fits him.
explanation.definitionFit: Naipaul was a Nobel-winning novelist and travel writer, so he is a writer of books.

clue.text: Finally fit, a donor plays Twister

indicators.note: finally means at the end, so only the last letter is kept
to play with something is to move it around freely, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the final letter of 'fit'
taken as written

explanation.walkthrough: The capital T makes Twister the party game, but it is a whirlwind.
explanation.definitionFit: Twister is an informal American word for a whirling storm column, which is a tornado.

clue.text: Instantly suspicious of a path to hatred

blocks.note: taken as written
